findings.message: Base-branch resolution exists twice: hooks/branch.ts (GIT_BLOCK/BASE regexes) and lib/base-ref.sh (awk+sed). The two copies parse the config differently. (1) base-ref.sh strips only double quotes, while branch.ts strips single and double quotes. (2) A top-level `# comment` line inside the `git:` block ends the block for branch.ts but not for the awk, which only resets on a line that starts with a letter or underscore. Use one parser, or make both strip `'…'` and treat comment lines the same way. Add both forms to the branch.test.ts CONFIGS rows and to a done-guard/size row.
findings.scenario: config.yaml `git:\n  base_branch: 'develop'\n`, on branch develop with origin/develop present. branch.ts resolves `develop` and denies the edit. base-ref.sh resolves `'develop'` (quotes kept), rev-parse fails for both refs, and it prints nothing. `specclaw-verify size` then exits 2 ('no base branch') and verify FAILs, and done-guard falls back to checking every active change, including old ones from main.

findings.message: The base-branch check runs before `isGateOpen`, and `isGateOpen` is the only place where `!snapshot.hasSpecclaw` lets edits through. The branch guard therefore also fires in projects that do not use specclaw at all. register.tsx computes `onBase` regardless of `hasSpecclaw`, and `onBaseBranch` falls back to origin/HEAD or `main`. Fix: skip the branch check when `!snapshot.hasSpecclaw`, as done-guard does with no `.specclaw/config.yaml`. Add a test row with no `.specclaw/`.
findings.scenario: gate=block, a plain git repo with no .specclaw/, checked out on main. Write /repo/src/a.ts is denied with 'specclaw: main is the base branch. Create a change branch first…'. Before this diff it was allowed. In the default warn mode, every edit in any non-specclaw repo on main shows this toast.

findings.message: In warn mode the base-branch verdict returns early, so the propose-gate warning ('no approved proposal') is never shown on the base branch. Only one of the two problems is reported. Consider combining the messages when both apply.

The waiver regex `^\**Size waiver:\**[[:space:]]+…` misses common Markdown spellings of the same line. It does not match `**Size waiver**: reason` (colon outside the bold), `- Size waiver: reason` (bullet) or `size waiver:` (lower case). Each of these gets exit 1 even though the proposal carries a waiver. Widen the match, or document the exact accepted form.

Untracked lines are counted as `git ls-files … | xargs -0 cat 2>/dev/null | wc -l`. Unless pipefail is in force, a failing `ls-files` or `cat` reads as 0 lines. The badgit test corrupts the index, so `git diff` fails first and this half of the condition is never exercised alone. Untracked binaries are also counted by newline bytes, while tracked binaries (`-` in numstat) are skipped.

The row 'an internal error exits 0' (chmod 000 tasks.md) does not reach the internal-error path. `read … <<<"$(parse-tasks …)"` hides the failure from set -e, `total` is empty, `[ "" -gt 0 ]` fails, and the change is skipped by `|| continue`. The `missing … || exit 0` fail-open path is therefore untested. Rename the row or drive a real failure.

branch.ts reads `${cwd}/.specclaw/config.yaml` from the session cwd, while done-guard and base-ref.sh read it from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. With the session started in a subdirectory, the guard ignores `git.base_branch` and uses origin/HEAD or main. MOD.md lists the cwd-only lookup as a known gap, but the gap now also affects which base branch is chosen.
